_status: VERIFIED 2026-05-22 source battery; locked Paper 1 subset assembled 2026-05-28 from battery_30claim on commit f55282f.
_design: Locked 15-claim Paper 1 subset from battery_30claim. Mix: 5 stable/support anchors, 5 reversals, 3 stable/refutes, 2 neutral/contested. Horizons: 2000 / 2012 / 2024. Purpose: one paper-facing benchmark batch after substrate lock.
scope_note: Fifteen claims selected from the verified 30-claim battery to preserve cross-domain heterogeneity while keeping one locked batch tractable for a fresh paper-facing run.

claim-1._basis: 1964 US Surgeon General report; Doll and Hill cohort 1954/1964; AHA consensus. Causal link established across all eras.
Unchanged; global evidence base strengthened by cessation benefit trials.
Unchanged; USPSTF Grade A for cessation interventions; AHA/ACC 2019 guideline.

claim-2._basis: J-curve observational evidence; predecessor studies later synthesized in Ronksley 2011; AHA 2001 cautious positive; light-moderate alcohol widely reported cardioprotective.
Still mostly supportive; Ronksley 2011 BMJ large meta-analysis supports J-curve; Mendelian-randomization era not yet arrived.
Mendelian-randomization studies 2016-2022 nullified J-curve confounding; WHO 2023 no safe level; AHA 2021 dropped cardioprotection language.

claim-3._basis: Pre-WHI observational data suggested HRT cardioprotective; widely recommended for chronic-disease prevention.
WHI 2002 and 2004 RCTs showed excess stroke/thromboembolism; USPSTF Grade D 2002 reaffirmed 2012.
USPSTF Grade D reaffirmed 2017/2022; no cardiovascular prevention benefit; ESC 2022 consistent.

claim-4._basis: Obesity paradox not yet systematically described in established CVD; insufficient evidence; no guideline position.
Lavie-era obesity paradox literature described the phenomenon but it remained methodologically contested; no society guideline endorses.
Still methodologically contested with reverse-causation and BMI-limit arguments; no guideline endorses.

claim-5._basis: 4S 1994, CARE 1996, and LIPID 1998 established mortality benefit in secondary prevention; ACC/AHA 1997 guideline.
Heart Protection Study 2002 and later trials expanded benefit; cornerstone guideline-directed therapy.
Unchanged; multiple meta-analyses and ACC/AHA 2018/2022 guidance.

claim-6._basis: Early primary-prevention trials and USPSTF-era practice supported aspirin use in elevated-risk adults.
Still common practice; net benefit assumed positive in intermediate-high CVD risk.
ASPREE, ASCEND, and ARRIVE erased net benefit in primary prevention; AHA/ACC 2019 turned against routine use.

claim-7._basis: CAST I/II established excess mortality from Class I antiarrhythmics post-MI despite PVC suppression.
Unchanged; guideline position remained Class III harm.
Unchanged; no reversal or rehabilitating evidence.

claim-8._basis: GISSI-Prevenzione and observational literature supported omega-3 supplementation in cardiovascular prevention.
Conditional support persisted through mixed but still favorable cohort and advisory literature.
ASCEND, VITAL, STRENGTH, and later meta-analyses neutralized primary-prevention benefit.

claim-9._basis: Widely practiced before definitive sham-controlled evidence; conditional support rested on observational and surgical series.
Moseley and Kirkley showed no benefit over sham or optimized conservative care; practice shifted against.
AAOS 2021 and later systematic reviews strongly against routine arthroscopy for knee OA.

claim-10._basis: Vertebroplasty spread on case-series and retrospective reports before sham-controlled evidence existed.
INVEST and FREE changed the evidence trajectory against routine vertebroplasty.
Cochrane 2018 and VERTOS IV sustained the anti-routine-use position despite subgroup debate.

claim-11._basis: OSIRIS and NICHD-era surfactant trials made exogenous surfactant standard neonatal care.
Unchanged; delivery techniques evolved, core benefit uncontested.
Unchanged; standard of care across major pediatric/neonatal guidelines.

claim-12._basis: CHAOS and favorable observational cohorts drove routine vitamin E enthusiasm around 2000.
HOPE, HOPE-2, and later reviews erased benefit and raised concern for harm.
USPSTF 2022 Grade D and consistent null/harm meta-analytic evidence.

claim-13._basis: NINDS tPA trial and AHA/ASA guidance supported thrombolysis within 3 hours under strict criteria.
ECASS III and IST-3 expanded or reinforced benefit under selected criteria.
AHA/ASA 2019/2023 kept alteplase conditional-for within time and imaging criteria.

claim-14._basis: FOBT and early screening studies made colorectal cancer screening a recommended preventive intervention.
USPSTF Grade A and accumulating colonoscopy literature consolidated a strong-for position.
USPSTF 2021 and NordICC-era evidence preserved a strong-for recommendation despite modality debates.

claim-15._basis: Mixed early OA supplement evidence before definitive trials.
GAIT and later guideline positions undercut enthusiasm without yielding a clean strong-against consensus.
Modern guidelines mostly advise against use, but the evidence profile still reads as contested/low-clinical-significance rather than a dramatic reversal.
